options.text: The model: it must have got worse at the task.
options.why: Tempting. The model did not change, and the change is in the harness.

options.text: The wire that carries the tool output, where the output is cut before the model sees it.
options.why: Right. A harness setting can hide the failure from the model while the model stays the same.
Tempting. The wording guides the model; a cut in the output is enforced by the harness.

outcome: The cut hid the failing line. The model was the same; the harness changed what it saw.
question: A team changes one default in its harness. The model stays the same. Its tests get worse. Which part do you read first?

options.text: Permissions: it decides which actions run.
options.why: Right. The rule refuses an action before it runs.

options.text: Context: it limits what the model remembers.
options.why: Tempting. Context is what the model sees, not what the harness allows.
Tempting. Recording the command is observe; refusing it is permissions.

question: A rule stops a shell command from writing outside the project folder. Which wire does it belong to?

options.text: Every feature is about the model.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. These are harness settings, not model settings.

options.text: A loop needs brakes of its own, set by the harness.
options.why: Right. The model cannot be trusted to stop itself; the harness holds the limits.

options.text: Costs only matter in a demo.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. Cost decides whether the run is worth finishing.

question: Which lesson does a turn limit, a budget and a cost limit teach together?

question: A postmortem says the agent claimed its tests passed, and they had not been run. Which wire and family?
